question.text: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> executes a simple harmonic motion under a periodic force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>–</mo><mn>25</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The particle attains a maximum speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> during its oscillation. The amplitude of the motion is ______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Given, force F=(–25x) N

⇒0.25a=-25x

⇒a=-100x

Now comparing it with standard equation, a=-ω2x we get

ω=10.

Now, vmax=ωA

⇒ωA=4

⇒A=410=0.4 m

⇒A=40 cm.
